_about: State 1 of the vocabulary of roles: the defined controllers of MIDI 1.0 that set a sound, each written as a part and a setting. A term cites in `source` every controller whose composition uses it. The names of MIDI 2.0 Property Exchange enter in a later state, once read at their piece.

terms.name: voice
terms.definition: The sound generator that plays one note at a time or several, before its filter and its output.

terms.name: sound
terms.definition: The sound as a whole, what a program recalls.

terms.name: filter
terms.definition: A filter that shapes the harmonic content of the sound.

terms.name: envelope
terms.definition: An envelope that shapes the level of the sound over the life of a note.

terms.name: output
terms.definition: The output of the instrument, where the sound leaves it.

terms.name: effect
terms.definition: An effect unit, numbered when the instrument has several.

terms.name: portamento-time
terms.definition: How long a note takes to glide to the next one.

terms.name: portamento
terms.definition: Whether notes glide from one to the next, on or off.

terms.name: portamento-start
terms.definition: The note from which the next glide starts.

terms.name: variation
terms.definition: Which variation of the sound plays, among those it holds.

terms.name: resonance
terms.definition: How much the filter emphasises the frequencies around its cutoff.

terms.name: cutoff
terms.definition: The frequency above which the filter lets less of the sound through.

terms.name: attack-time
terms.definition: How long the envelope takes to rise when a note starts.

terms.name: release-time
terms.definition: How long the envelope takes to fall when a note ends.

terms.name: balance
terms.definition: How the output leans between its left and right sides.

terms.name: pan
terms.definition: Where the output sits between left and right.

terms.name: expression
terms.definition: A level that scales the output within the level already set.

terms.name: depth
terms.definition: How much of the sound goes to the effect.
